cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron, the priest. This time the subject is the human body. Buckle up, friend, because Leviticus does NOT do small talk.

cards.question: Who are Moses and Aaron supposed to pass this message on to?

cards.text: Here's the first case: any man who has a bodily discharge. Friend, God is not being shy about this, so I won't be either.

cards.question: When any man has a bodily discharge, what does God say the discharge is?

cards.text: Flowing or blocked, his discharge brings about uncleanness. And it doesn't stay with him: any bed he lies on and any furniture he sits on becomes unclean too.

cards.question: Someone touches the bed of the man with the discharge. What must that person do?

answers.text: Wash his clothes and bathe with water
Shave off all his hair and his beard
Stay outside the camp for a whole week

cards.text: Sit where he sat, touch his body, or get spit on by him, and it's the same thing: wash, bathe, unclean until evening. Friend, in that camp your clothes got washed MORE than they got worn.

cards.question: True or false: a saddle the man with the discharge rides on stays clean.

cards.text: Whoever touches anything that was under him is unclean until evening. And whoever just CARRIES those things? Wash and bathe, friend. Even the moving crew gets no pass.

cards.question: The man with the discharge touches someone. When does that person have to wash and bathe?

answers.text: When he didn't rinse his hands first
When he touched them after dark
When he touched them on the Sabbath

cards.text: Now the law walks right into the kitchen. And friend, as a kitchen tool myself, I am holding my BREATH.

cards.question: Any clay pot the man with the discharge touches must be ___.
True or false: a wooden utensil the man with the discharge touches must be broken too.

cards.text: Then the good news: the man is cleansed from his discharge, and he counts off seven days. Believe me, I counted the dust in a junk drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: After counting off his seven days, the cleansed man washes his clothes. What does he bathe himself in?

cards.text: On the eighth day, he comes before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, bringing two birds. Eight days of counting, friend, and I bet he was FIRST in line.

cards.question: On the eighth day, who does the cleansed man give his two birds to?
The priest sacrifices the man's two birds. What are they offered as?

answers.text: A sin offering and a burnt offering
A guilt offering and a grain offering
A peace offering and a wave offering

cards.text: In this way the priest makes atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge. He isn't left stuck, friend: the way through is written right there.
Next case, and the law keeps it plain, so I will too. When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water.

cards.question: True or false: after an emission of semen, the man brings two birds to the priest on the eighth day.

cards.text: Any clothing or leather with semen on it gets washed with water and stays unclean until evening. Then the law covers a man and a woman together, and it doesn't blink, friend.

cards.question: True or false: if a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, only the man has to bathe.

cards.text: Now the law turns to women. When a woman has her flow of blood, she is unclean due to her menstruation, and friend, I'm a cookie stamper, so I'm reading it straight and keeping my mustache OUT of it.

cards.question: A woman is unclean due to her menstruation for ___ days.
During a woman's period, what happens to anyone who touches her?

answers.text: They bring two birds to the priest

cards.text: Anything she lies or sits on during her period is unclean. Touch her bed or her furniture, and the laundry's back: wash, bathe, unclean until evening.
Then the law adds an "if": if a man lies with her and her flow touches him. Friend, I'll let the law do the talking on this one.

cards.question: True or false: if a man lies with a woman during her period and her flow touches him, he is unclean only until evening.

cards.text: Then a different case. A woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside her period, or it keeps going past it, and I bet that's a long, hard stretch, friend.

cards.question: How long is a woman with this kind of discharge unclean?

answers.text: All the days of her discharge

cards.text: Her bed and furniture are unclean, like her bed during her period. Touch them, and you know the drill by now, friend: wash, bathe, unclean until evening.

When she's cleansed, she counts off seven days, and on the eighth day she brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, who makes atonement for her before the LORD. Same eighth day, same doorway, same two birds, friend: if that sounds familiar, you were LISTENING.

cards.question: God finally gives the reason behind all of this. Why must the children of Israel be kept separate from their uncleanness?

answers.text: So they don't die by making His tabernacle unclean
So sickness doesn't spread from tent to tent
So the nations around them stay far away

cards.question: God calls it My tabernacle. True or false: He says it sits far off from the people.
The law closes by listing everyone it covers. True or false: it covers both males and females who have a discharge.

cards.text: The law wraps up by naming every case: the man with a discharge, the emission of semen, the woman's period, any male or female with a discharge, and a man who lies with an unclean woman. Not one case left out, friend, and like I said, Leviticus does NOT do small talk.

findings.problem: The card identifies Moses as Israel's leader and Aaron as his brother and the priest, but its only reference is Leviticus 15:1, which merely names Moses and Aaron. These outside-passage facts need supporting references.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Seven of the ten choice cards are multiple choice, while only two are true or false and one is fill in the blank. Multiple choice therefore dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card runs to four sentences: the statement about touching things, the question about carrying them, the command to wash and bathe, and the moving-crew punchline.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Eight days of counting" contradicts the passage. Leviticus 15:13 says to count off seven days, and verse 14 then describes what happens on the eighth day.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "This kind of discharge" depends on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible. Because the passage covers several kinds of discharge, the question needs to explain that this is a discharge of blood lasting many days outside or beyond the woman's period.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.
